newsitem.title: USA: Texas "Cheerleader Mom" goes to jail for murder plot.
newsitem.headline: Texas "Cheerleader Mom" goes to jail for murder plot.

text.p: A Texas woman who allegedly hired a hit man to kill the mother of her daughter's cheerleading rival was sentenced to prison on Monday after pleading no contest to a murder-for-hire charge.

Wanda Holloway, who became known as the "Cheerleader Mom" in a case that drew worldwide attention, was sentenced to 10 years in jail but will be freed on probation in less than six months under terms of the plea agreement, her attorney said.
"She's going to jail and she's going to have to pay for her crime," Verna Heath, the target of the murder-for-hire scheme, told reporters.

Holloway allegedly planned the murder to unsettle Heath's daughter Amber, a rival of daughter Shanna Holloway, for a spot on their junior high school cheerleading squad in Channelview, a refinery town near Houston.

Holloway was initially convicted and sentenced to 15 years in prison on charges of solicitation of capital murder in 1991, but that sentence was tossed out because one of the jurors was later found to have a criminal record.
"Nobody was hurt in this case and it was a weak case in the first place," said attorney Jack Zimmermann, who was representing Holloway in a second trial set to start in October.
